Peters's epauletted fruit bat (Micropteropus pusillus) is a small pteropodid that exhibits a relatively rapid life history for an African megabat. This altricial pup is entirely dependent on maternal milk during the initial weeks postpartum. Under the stable thermal conditions typical of the species' roosting environment (34.5 °C [T = 34.5 °C]), the weaning period is relatively brief; young achieve nutritional independence after about 50 days since birth [tx = about 50 days since birth], a duration derived from comparative data on the congener Eidolon helvum that has been adjusted for the pronounced difference in adult body size between the two species. The suckling juvenile therefore transitions to solid food relatively quickly, allowing females to invest in subsequent reproductive bouts without an extended period of lactational demand.

The ultimate wet body mass attained by adult males of this species is approximately 35 grams [Wwi = approximately 35 grams], placing Micropteropus pusillus among the smaller fruit bats in its sub-Saharan African range. This modest adult size has important consequences for its reproductive biology and energy budget. The gestating embryo undergoes a protracted period of organogenesis and foetal growth, after which the female gives birth to a single, well-developed altricial neonate. The relatively extended gestation, when considered alongside the small litter size, is consistent with a strategy that prioritizes offspring quality and post-natal survival over maximizing the number of young produced per breeding attempt. This investment is further reflected in the species' overall pace of life, which favors longevity over rapid generational turnover.

Sexual maturation in female Peters's epauletted fruit bats is a gradual process, with puberty typically attained at approximately 183 days since birth [tp = approximately 183 days since birth] under the species' habitual roost temperature of 34.5 °C [T = 34.5 °C]. Longevity records for Micropteropus pusillus suggest a maximum lifespan in the wild of approximately 21.8 years [am = approximately 21.8 years] at the standard roosting temperature of 34.5 °C [T = 34.5 °C], a value extrapolated from demographic data for the larger congener Eidolon helvum.
